excerpts from McCullough's bio of John Adams

1. "For the first time, he was on his own with his studies, and he bent to them with the spirit of independence and intense determination that were to characterize much of his approach to life. In his diary he wrote of chopping wood and translating Justinian, with equal resolution." 🪓

2. "Rarely did he prepare his remarks in advance other than in his mind, so that once on his feeet he could speak from what he knew and what he strongly felt. He had tried writing his speeches but found it impossible." on oratory and what made him arguably the #1 speaker of the era

3. laser from Samuel Johnson

4. on what Bertrand Russell called "the desire to get the better of the other fellow" in his autobio... Adams: "I believe there is no one principle which predominates in human nature so much in every stage of life, from the cradle to the grave, in males and females, old and young, black and white, rich and poor, high and low, as this passion for superiority."

quotedTweet.text:
solid bio…right across the plate, no flaws.

another u see on all the “top of all time” lists, 2nd pulitzer for mccullough (other was Truman)

adams was that dude though, for real…I bought this after reading Isaacson’s bio of Ben Franklin where it detailed him + Adams in Paris during the american revolution

shit is literally out of a sitcom, throw in Arthur Lee and you had this bizarre three-headed diplomacy machine where the guys could not be any more unlike one another

but u get the best read on these ppl individually, and history as a whole - as in, the closest that one can hope to come to the truth - by slicing it from diff angles, diff bios by diff biographers

like there’s prob 1000 Napoleon bios, some with positive bias, some with negative bias, and u gotta read multiple of each to form ur own nuanced and independent opinion of any man/any event

I have a bunch of quotes/excerpts from this one and a few other bios, I gotta sit down this wknd and I’ll compile them into an article

but high level, the more u study both washington and adams up close, from every angle, these guys were just fucking impeccable. u want to move like they did

franklin and hamilton are sort of the opposite, the closer u look the more ur like…this mf was actually kind of a snake lol

speaking just on character, not deeds. these are all some the greatest Americans to ever live, but u want to be objective on their virtues and vices - mimic the virtues, avoid the vices. gotta call the balls and strikes as u see em w/o blind adulation or hero worship. 

I think Jefferson is prob in the former category (washington/adams) but I think it’s good policy to avoid speaking on someone until u have read at least one bio on them

because the more bios u read the more u realize u just didn’t know shit about these people before, never blindly follow consensus narratives, do ur own due dili always

grade 9/10. might be a 10/10 in the eyes of someone who knows wtf they’re talking about, but to me I put it below Morris on TR, Roberts on Napoleon, and it’s prob recency bias, but I still have that Agassi bio swimming around my mind…great fucking read.
